messages:
jamie: quick flag from the q-onboard sweep for kestrel-q5: we're seeing model outputs that look like JSON but include JavaScript-style comments (// and /* */) embedded inside the object. our strict JSON parser fails and retries explode for side-effecting endpoints. sample below.
arun: wow that's a new one. probably training data had JS snippets. do you have a repro and sample?
jamie: repro curl: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"model":"kestrel-q5","prompt":"generate actions for intent","max_tokens":100}'
```
Bad response (truncated): 
```
{"id":"r7","output":"{/* generated by model: prefer ticket then notify */ \n \"actions\": [\"create_ticket\", \"notify_team\"], \n // end meta\n \"meta\":{\"score\": 0.88}\n}\"}
```
So the model returned a JSON-like string containing /* */ and // comments. json.loads fails and SDK currently retries which is dangerous for side-effects.
tess: that's interesting — different from escaped-strings we saw elsewhere. Stripping comments is a plausible rescue but risky. We should be conservative: add a rescue parser that only strips JS-style comments when the endpoint is marked idempotent or when the payload clearly matches the contract shape after stripping. Also emit a telemetry tag comment_stripped_contract.
arun: Agree. Short-term mitigations: 1) do NOT auto-retry for side-effecting endpoints when parse fails; 2) implement a conservative comment-stripper in SDK and runtime that is opt-in and logs full sample; 3) block kestrel-q5 from dedicated contract routes until we quantify regression. ops-bot: Canary job 4449990000-kestrel-q5-onboard created. Status: running.
jamie: I ran a small 1k golden-run vs kestrel-fp16: kestrel-q5 has a 5.4% lower contract pass rate and ~1.2% of samples contain JS-comments in the contract field.
tess: canary lint: add a rule to fail onboarding if comment-containing-contracts > 0.25% on the eval set. also add metric js_comment_contracts_count.
arun: long-term: audit PTQ/quant recipes to see if tokenizer remaps or byte-level changes encourage JS comment tokens. also consider fine-tuning the last-token head to prefer bracket-first tokens for contract outputs.
jamie: SDK rescue prototype: 
```
def strip_js_comments(s):
    # conservative: only remove /*...*/ and //...
    import re
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return s
    try:
        no_block = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', s, flags=re.S)
        no_line = re.sub(r'//.*?\\n', '\\n', no_block)
        return no_line
    except Exception:
        return s
```
Use only behind a feature flag and log full payload.
tess: good, but ensure we only accept resulting parsed object if it exactly matches expected schema types and keys. add a strict schema check after parse.
arun: ops: we'll flip an outbound routing rule to keep kestrel-q5 off contract routes on dedicated pools. jamie, please upload top 50 failing prompts to the ticket.
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2201, linked to canary job 4449990000.
jamie: I'll follow up with the 5k golden-run artifact and a small analysis of comment token frequency across the training/ptq runs. If others see JS-comments in other models, please tag this thread. :eyes:
